inspiration: test_call_return_variable_folding; angr call-return variable folding (expression folding in angr/analyses/decompiler); print_long_format

decisions.question: safety predicate for which call outputs are order-safe to fold, and scope (small vs large)
decisions.safety_predicate: Fold (mark implied) iff the call output has exactly one non-marker descendant (lone_descend is Some), that use op lives in the SAME basic block as the call op AND is not a CPUI_MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT marker, and no op strictly between the call and its use in that block's op order is a CPUI_CALL/CALLIND/CALLOTHER/STORE/LOAD (or any op flagged is_call); otherwise leave explicit.
decisions.reasoning: Making a call output implied physically relocates the call's evaluation down to its single use site, so correctness reduces to proving nothing observable is reordered across that move: same-block confines the move to a linear op sequence; the no-intervening-side-effect scan guards the only ops whose relative order with a call is observable. Keeping LOAD in the forbidden set is necessary (read-after-write: the call may STORE memory an intervening LOAD reads). Forbidding marker use ops is consistent with base_explicit returning explicit for marker DEFs. The predicate strictly tightens the printer's pre-existing single-use inlining, preferring false negatives over reordering bugs.
decisions.scope_justification: One new module (kuna_callretfold.rs: predicate + option) and one gated early-return branch inside one ported-core anchor (base_explicit in s6_variables/coreaction_cleanup.rs). The remaining edits are the identical on/off flag plumbing every simple option carries (seams.rs/architecture.rs/options.rs/stages.toml). No new pass type, no infrastructure, zero S7 code -> small, implement now.
